featured_videos.title: Jillian Michaels: "Eat Beef Once A Month"
featured_videos.creator: Kent Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: Jillian Michaels: "Eat Beef Once A Month"
featured_videos.commentary: Jillian Michaels telling people to eat beef once a month is wild when you've got community members here saying two steaks a day changed their life. The gap between what mainstream fitness personalities push and what actually works for our readers is getting harder to ignore. The comments nailing her track record from The Biggest Loser say it all. if her approach was optimal, those contestants wouldn't have gained everything back. This is the thing about old-school fitness advice: it sounds reasonable on the surface, but real people reporting real results (and real struggles with the approach she promotes) tell a different story.

featured_videos.title: Perché dopo aver ELIMINATO i CARBOIDRATI hai il COLESTEROLO LDL ALTO?
featured_videos.creator: The Carnivore Way
featured_videos.editorial_title: Perché dopo aver ELIMINATO i CARBOIDRATI hai il COLESTEROLO LDL ALTO?
featured_videos.commentary: This video hits on the biggest worry I hear from people starting carnivore, and the comments show why the conversation matters so much. Someone here has an LDL of 380 but feels better, their HDL is solid, and their triglycerides are dirt low, which tells a completely different story than that single number ever could. The real insight these comments keep circling back to is particle size and oxidation, not just the total LDL count, which is exactly what I covered in our piece on cholesterol on carnivore. Your doctor seeing LDL go up and reaching for statins without looking at HDL, triglycerides, and inflammation markers is missing half the picture, and that's the gap this video is trying to close.

featured_videos.title: Costco Meat Hack: This Budget Friendly Steak You May Have Never Tried
featured_videos.creator: Laura Spath
featured_videos.editorial_title: Costco Meat Hack: This Budget Friendly Steak You May Have Never Tried
featured_videos.commentary: Okay, so community is saying picanha is genuinely hard to find where they live, and then someone in Texas casually mentions their HEB always has them cut up and ready to go. That's the vibe right now. Budget-friendly cuts that actually taste incredible are spreading through Costco locations, and people are excited because they're learning there's more to steak than ribeye markup prices. The fat cap on picanha is doing the heavy lifting here, rendering down and basically basting the meat as it cooks. If you're looking to maximize flavor without the ribeye price tag, this is exactly the kind of practical grocery hack our audience has been asking about for meal prep budgeting.

featured_videos.title: Why JD Vance Won’t Say the Word Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: HomeSteadHow
featured_videos.editorial_title: Why JD Vance Won’t Say the Word Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: The comments here tell the real story. People are losing 90 pounds in six months, healing their psoriasis, ditching anxiety and depression, and the response from family and society is. hostility. That's not about the science. That's about the culture war around meat, and Vance knows it. He's not staying quiet because carnivore doesn't work, he's staying quiet because saying it out loud invites the kind of verbal attacks that one commenter described from his own brother. The irony is thick: the diet is working, but the word itself has become politically radioactive. For anyone here feeling alone in your food choices, you're not crazy, and you're not alone. The results speak louder than the pushback ever will.

featured_videos.title: Carnivore is Out, Fibermaxxing is In
featured_videos.creator: Unnatural Vegan
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivore is Out, Fibermaxxing is In
featured_videos.commentary: Unnatural Vegan's point about fiber lands, but here's what she's missing: the carnivore crowd isn't "out," they're just not posting about it anymore. The real story is that fibermaxxing solves a problem carnivore created for some people (constipation, bloating, nutrient gaps), and that's actually useful data, not a trend reversal. What's funny is how the comments prove her own case. people casually hitting 25-50g of fiber without trying, just by eating whole foods. That's the boring answer nobody wants to hear. Protocol beats trends, whether you're counting grams of protein or grams of fiber.

featured_videos.title: This Carnivore Pizza Pocket Feels Like a Cheat Meal
featured_videos.creator: Meet Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: This Carnivore Pizza Pocket Feels Like a Cheat Meal
featured_videos.commentary: I love that the top comment calls this a calzone, because that's exactly what people need to hear. you're not inventing something fake or forcing yourself to eat sad "carnivore approved" substitutes. You're making real food that happens to fit the way you eat now. The bulk-freezing comments show what I've seen work over and over in my coaching: simple recipes that scale become the difference between sticking with carnivore long-term or burning out. This feels like a cheat meal because it *tastes* like one, which matters way more than pretending you don't miss certain foods.
